definition: Estimating the risk of patient death from clinical data — used in ICU scoring systems and requiring careful calibration and fairness review.
details: Estimating the risk of patient death from clinical data — used in ICU scoring systems and requiring careful calibration and fairness review.

explainer.lead: Mortality prediction estimates the risk of patient death from clinical data. It is used in ICU scoring systems and demands careful calibration and fairness review.

tiers.eli5: It is a risk score that says how likely a very sick patient is to die, so care teams can act.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers build models on clinical data for ICU scoring. The common pitfall is trusting raw scores without checking calibration and fairness across patient groups.
tiers.paperLevel: Estimating death risk from clinical data; requires calibration assessment and fairness review, since poorly calibrated or biased outputs mislead decisions.

explainer.example: An ICU scoring model outputs a death-risk estimate for a patient, which is checked for calibration before use.
